_what_this_is: Measurements taken for #122 (FluidAudio 0.15.4 -> 0.15.5), together with their scope, provenance and reproduction caveats. Higher-level conclusions are in the CHANGELOG entry, which cites this file.
_reproducing: Recomputable from what is recorded here: the corpus hashes; both arms' transcript hashes; the nm counts; `corpus_duration_seconds` (the corpora registry); `fluidaudio_revision` (Package.resolved); and `metric` — for which the reference is an SRT, so the path is `SRTParser.parse` then `SRTParser.referenceText(from:)` on it, and only then this repo's `TextNormalizer` and `ErrorRate.wer`. Feeding the .srt file's raw text in instead gives edits=6 / ref_words=83 / wer=0.0722 rather than the recorded 0.0375. Not recomputable: `executable_sha256` (see its note); `measured_at` / `machine` / `toolchain`, which are observations of one run; and all of `path_coverage`, which needs the instrumentation `path_coverage.how` describes. The path_coverage counts have each been produced independently by more than one party; the verification comments on PR #142 link those runs.

session.toolchain: Apple Swift 6.2.4 (swift-6.2.4-RELEASE), the PATH default on this machine
session.toolchain_caveat: `swift build -c release` crashes under this toolchain — SIL memory lifetime failure in OwnershipModelEliminator compiling swift-transformers' Tokenizers, unrelated to FluidAudio. scripts/install.sh documents the same crash as "SIL specialization"; this description is the more precise of the two. These are debug builds, which is why the nm counts under `arms` are debug counts.
session.transcribe_command: <realpath .build/arm64-apple-macosx/debug/bestasr> transcribe <audio> --backend fluid-parakeet --model 0.6b-v3 --language en --hallucination-filter off --format srt --output <out.srt>   # and again with `--format txt --output <out.txt>`; two invocations, one per format
notes: `transcribe`, not `benchmark`: benchmark writes to ~/.bestasr/store and has no --store-dir (issue #160), so it cannot run without touching durable user data. transcribe reads the store for routing and writes nothing.
Invoked by realpath: `bestasr` is not resolvable on PATH on this machine, so a bare `bestasr …` command string would not run at all.
--hallucination-filter off removes post-processing. Both formats because a moved seam shows up in SRT timecodes before it shows up in words.
Two runs per pin. This bounds decoder variability rather than excluding it: no run-to-run difference was observed in four runs.

arms.cross_pin_cmp: srt identical, txt identical (byte comparison, not equal-WER)
arms._executable_hash_note: Recorded to identify the build these numbers came from, NOT as a reproducible value — the same pin built twice yields different hashes. Two purposes, two fields: the revision says which dependency source was expected, the hash says which artifact was measured.
arms._nm_note: This count varies with build configuration and nm flags. Measured cells: debug/plain 4, debug/-a 8 (toolchain in `session`); release/plain 2, release/-a 4 (Apple Swift 6.3.3, swiftlang-6.3.3.1.3, at /usr/bin/swift; Xcode 26.6 build 17F113; xcode-select -p = /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer; arm64) — the release cells needed a different toolchain because the one in `session` cannot build release at all. Across those four cells 0.15.4 was 0 and 0.15.5 was non-zero. No claim is made for other build settings, stripping, architectures or nm options. An earlier version recorded 4 without saying which build or flag produced it; a third party running plain nm on a release build got 2.

metric._note: Numerator and denominator recorded so the value can be re-derived. Identical on both arms, which follows from the transcripts being byte-identical.

path_coverage.how: stderr probes compiled into .build/checkouts/FluidAudio/…/TDT/ChunkProcessor.swift. Probed for the counts below: the case-fold branch of tokenIdsMatch (separating a fold match from a consultation whose canonicals differed from one where at least one id is absent from the map — three outcomes, and the third is most of the traffic); the entry and exit of collapseSeamWordDuplicates (token count in and out); and all three of 0ac0e414's word-boundary fallbacks — mergeUsingMatches' tail re-splice, popSeamWord's safe-id branch, and mergeByMidpoint's right-scan when it adopts an advanced cutoff. Probed as scaffolding rather than as a changed site: the merge loop, for the chunk and merge counts and to compute each merge a second time with caseVariantIds passed as nil, which reduces tokenIdsMatch to `left == right` — 0.15.4's matcher. Before believing any count, check that each of your own probe markers is in the binary — `strings "$exe" | grep -Fq -- "$marker"` per marker, failing hard on the first miss. That is a necessary check, not a sufficient one: it shows the literals are present, not that every probe site is, nor that any probe ran. A build that did not pick up the patch produces a probe-free binary whose output is trivially identical to the clean one, which reads as success. That happened once here. The cause was never isolated — an earlier version of this file blamed SwiftPM for refusing to recompile an edited checkout after the first build, and that is false: measured across three edit-then-build round-trips, it recompiles every time.
_limits: 375 and 518 are ' r' and ' R' in the vocabulary; 0.15.4's matcher returns false for that pair because it compares ids for equality.

"Entered" has two natural cut points, because the guard binds three conditions at once: reaching it (773) and passing it with both ids in the map (133). Say which one a count refers to. `case_folded_matches` is neither — it is the 2 times the branch returned a match. An earlier version of this file claimed two independent runs had reported irreconcilable decompositions and used that to withhold these numbers; they were consistent, and had taken different cut points.
collapse_tokens_in == collapse_tokens_out establishes that no token was removed. It does not by itself establish that ids, order or timestamps are unchanged.
The counterfactual isolates the incremental effect of supplying caseVariantIds inside a 0.15.5 binary. It is not a 0.15.4 execution, and it assumes the nil path is equivalent to 0.15.4's matcher.
The probe build's transcript hash equals the clean build's, so no final-output perturbation was observed. That does not establish that the instrumentation was control-flow-neutral.

store_note: An earlier 0.15.4 run wrote a measurements.jsonl row stamped app_version 0.16.0 — the version shipping with 0.15.5 — because the schema has no FluidAudio field, so the row could not say what condition produced it. That row was removed rather than left to be ranked against honest ones; a backup was kept at ~/.bestasr/store/measurements.jsonl.bak-idd122-20260803161704, which is machine-local and therefore not auditable from this repo. The measurements recorded here wrote nothing to the store — verified by hashing all five store files before and after.
